title: Full-control authority and profile model
objective: Implement and qualify the Deskal-owned authority model that makes user-selected full computer control possible without exposing any donor executor yet: Safe remains the default; Full User uses a locally granted FullControlLease; Full Admin requires a separate AdminLease backed only by legitimate Windows elevation; all full-control authority is identity-bound, revocable, expiring or explicitly session-scoped, auditable, and impossible for an agent, donor, relay, or remote caller to self-grant.

include: Safe, Full User, Full Admin, Persistent Admin intent, and Remote Full Control profile vocabulary and transition rules
FullControlLease and AdminLease typed contracts, stable IDs, issue/expiry/session lifetime, epoch, policy revision, device, Deskal session, Windows user, and logon-session binding
local-only grant, revoke, status, expiry, policy-invalidation, restart, and emergency-revoke semantics
capability/profile policy that states which future executor classes each authority mode may use without exposing those executors in this grain
audit-safe grant, revoke, expiry, invalidation, and denied-self-grant evidence
fail-closed result semantics for stale, expired, wrong-user, wrong-session, wrong-device, wrong-policy, revoked, unavailable-elevation, and remote-self-grant paths
native Windows qualification for user/logon-session identity binding where the implementation relies on Windows identity
exclude: importing Open Computer Use, Desktop Commander, Firecrawl, Agent Reach, UI-TARS, gsudo, or other donor runtime code
desktop screenshot, UIA actuation, mouse, keyboard, shell, process-session, expanded filesystem, browser-profile, web-scrape, crawl, search, or visual-agent executor exposure
installing or starting an elevated broker or Windows service
acquiring, caching, duplicating, or impersonating an elevated token
UAC bypass, Windows Hello bypass, secure-desktop automation, credential-provider bypass, SYSTEM, or TrustedInstaller authority
new caller-facing MCP tools that grant or mint full-control or admin authority

authority_delta.filesystem: None. Existing bounded filesystem authority remains unchanged.
authority_delta.process: None. Existing process authority remains unchanged.
authority_delta.approval: Adds Deskal-internal, local-user-controlled FullControlLease/AdminLease grant, revoke, expiry, and profile state. Agent, MCP, relay, donor, and remote callers cannot issue, widen, renew, or persist these leases.
authority_delta.privileged: Adds AdminLease intent and validation shape only. No elevated token acquisition, broker, service, privileged execution, UAC bypass, or administrator operation is introduced by SG-000093.

invariants: Safe is the default authority mode after install, restart, invalid state, or absent local grant.

FullControlLease is bound to the exact local Windows user, logon session, device identity, Deskal session, selected profile, policy revision, lease epoch, issue time, and expiry or explicit session lifetime.
AdminLease cannot be valid without a legitimate OS-issued elevated administrator token binding; SG-000093 does not acquire or host that token.
Persistent Admin remains disabled and unavailable until its dedicated successor grain closes canonically.
Remote Full Control remains unavailable for execution until its dedicated successor grain; a remote caller cannot create, widen, renew, persist, or convert any local full-control lease.
No model output, MCP argument, donor process, relay message, browser page, shell command, or remote principal can mint an authority lease.
Emergency revoke and policy/identity epoch changes invalidate affected leases before new mutation dispatch.
A stale, expired, revoked, wrong-user, wrong-session, wrong-device, wrong-policy, or unsupported lease fails closed and cannot silently fall back to broader authority.
SG-000093 does not expose donor executors or widen the current filesystem, process, browser, network, UI-input, remote, or privileged execution surface.
Mutations retain not_started, dispatched, completed, cancelled, and outcome_unknown semantics and are never auto-retried merely because a lease changed.

acceptance.claim: The canonical authority-mode and profile vocabulary contains exactly Safe, Full User, Full Admin, Persistent Admin, and Remote Full Control, with Safe the sole default.

FullControlLease is typed and cryptographically/unforgeably identified, is bound to local user/logon session/device/Deskal session/profile/policy/epoch/time, and fails closed on every binding mismatch.
Only the authenticated local user control path can grant or revoke Full User/Admin intent; agent, MCP, donor, relay, and remote paths have no lease-minting or lease-widening operation.
AdminLease requires proof of a legitimate elevated Windows authority binding but SG-000093 has no elevation broker, token acquisition, cached elevation, privileged service, or admin executor.
Emergency revoke, ordinary revoke, expiry, policy revision, identity/session change, and restart semantics deterministically invalidate the appropriate leases and block undispatched mutations.
Profile rules are explicit for future desktop, shell/process, filesystem, browser, web, visual-agent, admin, and remote executor classes, but no successor executor becomes callable in this grain.
Persistent Admin remains unavailable and Remote Full Control remains execution-disabled; neither can be inferred from prior Full User or Full Admin use.
Unit, integration, adversarial self-grant, stale-binding, revoke, and native Windows identity/session tests pass on the exact head with no secret/token material written to ordinary logs or evidence.
The exact implementation diff imports no donor runtime code, adds no new privileged service, and does not widen existing MCP tool exposure.

successor_requirements.sg_000094: SG-000094 may activate only after SG-000093 closes canonically. It may import/adapt the pinned Open Computer Use Windows host only behind private Deskal IPC and may expose observation/capture host mechanics, but desktop input remains for SG-000095.

done_when: The user-selectable full-control authority model is implemented and qualified inside Deskal with Safe default, exact lease/profile binding, local-only grants, deterministic revoke/expiry/emergency-stop behavior, no self-grant path, no donor executor exposure, and no privileged broker yet.
